items.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: I think mainly what I remember best it seems that he had the most records of people like Jack Teagarden, Max Kaminsky, Bud Freeman, the Chicago guys

ctx.x: That’s right. We’ve got to get things rolling somehow. It seems interesting to look at your career and know that you started playing Dixieland and went about as far on the spectrum as you could it seems like.

Yeah. My father and those records that I was telling you about were the first music that I heard, in the home. And I think basically that’s what it was, there was Louis Armstrong and Jelly Roll Morton and some New Orleans characters in there too, but I think mainly what I remember best it seems that he had the most records of people like Jack Teagarden, Max Kaminsky, Bud Freeman, the Chicago guys, Duke Ellington in the ‘30s kind of records, late ‘20s and ‘30s. Because don’t forget, I wasn’t born until ‘35 so when…
